**Wake the target worker when a table delivery is queued.** When `tryPush()` returns false, `deliver()` writes the frame to the target worker's deliver table. That write sends no wake. While the target worker's wake subscriber is healthy, its held-open loop parks until a Redis wake or a scheduled deadline. The table frame can then wait up to the five-second safety poll instead of the previous 0.2-second tick. A frame in the deliver table must reach the client within the held-open tick while the subscriber is healthy. Either notify the target worker when the table entry is written, or service the deliver table at a short interval regardless of subscriber health. A Redis-based notification uses the pool that failed in this case, so it can fail too. Keep the long idle waits for the successful Redis wake path.

Review comment at @src/Application/Service/Async/SseServer.php at line 745: Update the held-open wait flow around waitForWork so a deliver-table frame is serviced within HELD_OPEN_TICK_SECONDS even when wakeHealthy is true. Use a notification path that does not depend on the Redis pool that failed, or check the deliver table at the short interval while preserving long idle waits after successful Redis wakes. After applying the fix, consider running `coderabbit review --agent` for local review. Visit https://docs.coderabbit.ai/cli?utm_source=ghpr ```

Fixed in 37927aa. It is a regression of this PR: the table path is taken exactly when Redis refused the frame, so no wake can be published, and the owner's loop stayed parked until the 5 s safety poll. queueForWorker() now bumps a counter row for the target worker in the deliver table; the wake subscriber's 0.2 s per-worker timer reads that one cell and, only when it moved, scans the table and wakes the sessions that have a frame there. That wake does not mark Redis dirty, so it costs no pop; an idle worker never scans and the long idle waits are unchanged. Test: HeldOpenLoopIdleRedisTest::a_frame_parked_in_the_deliver_table_reaches_a_parked_loop_on_the_next_tick (errors on 42c4c75, where the seam does not exist).

`@syntaxwanderer` Thanks for the fix. One case remains: if the target worker has no signal row and the deliver table cannot allocate one because its collision space is exhausted, `queueForWorker()` can insert the frame but fail to increment the signal. It ignores that failure at `SseWorkerTables.php` Line 318. The owner can then remain parked until a scheduled poll. Please reserve signal rows or otherwise handle signal allocation failure, and add a regression test for that case. The current test calls `wakeTableDeliveries()` directly, so it does not verify the timer path. I could not run the tests in this sandbox, and I’m not marking the finding as addressed. ---
